# Thunder Spike

## Setup

2026-07-15, RECOUNT measurement pair. Character level 85, hero Erika (Lightning Shadow trait base tier 1 — this trait is the source of the build's Numbed Effect bonus, not gear/talents), Thunder Spike Lv20, weapon: white "Unforgotten Long Blade" only (154-154 Physical implicit, 1.5 APS, 500 crit rating), no other gear/talents. Target: Lv85 training dummy (see `training-dummy.json`). Setup A: bare Thunder Spike, no supports. Setup B: Setup A + Level 20 Haunt support. Comparison target is the Recount span-average DPS ONLY — per `training-dummy.json`'s own doctrine, the character-sheet tooltip is not a verification source (see notes).

## Raw data points

Setup A (solo): Recount Average DPS 349 (2:17 span). Numbed: flat 1 stack — only the player's own True Body hit applies it in this config (no shadows present).

Setup B (+ Haunt Lv20): Recount Average DPS 810 (2:00 span). Numbed: alternates 1↔2 stacks, ~50% uptime on 2 (avg ≈1.5) — the extra stacks come from Haunt's shadows also applying Thunder Spike's inherent on-hit Numbed (see notes, NEW mechanic).

**Vs-target agreement, Recount only (validates base WAD; supports the intrinsic conversion + inherent on-hit Numbed in aggregate):** solo engine 340.34 vs measured 349 = **−2.5%** (flat-1-stack model, no correction applies — solo genuinely runs at 1 stack, so this is the honest residual: crit RNG / measurement noise / a small conservative bias). Haunt config: engine 789.03 vs measured 810 = −2.6% at the flat-1-stack baseline; corrected for the observed ~1.5-average-stack Numbed uplift, 811.01 (+0.1%). The Haunt correction is the model change here — solo is NOT corrected, since solo never leaves 1 stack.

**Numbed model, quantified:** predicted uplift ≈5.9%/stack at 18% Numbed Effect (`0.05 × 1.18`); applied to the Haunt run's ~1.5-average-stack observation, this closes most of the −2.6% Haunt gap (789.03 → 811.01, +0.1%) — a close match on the per-stack Numbed magnitude, isolated from the WAD/conversion question above since it's a same-run correction.

**Owner-reported in-game observation (2026-07-15), Haunt run only: Numbed stacks alternate 1↔2 in-game, with ~50% uptime on 2 stacks** (avg ≈1.5). The engine deliberately models a flat 1 stack (see `implementation`) — this is a known, now-quantified conservative bias of roughly −2.6% on a Haunt-equipped (shadow-present) baseline; it is NOT a bias on a shadow-free baseline like solo, where flat-1 is exact. Model the alternation only if ailment-uptime + shadow-hit modeling both land (see `docs/BACKLOG.md` §0f and the NEW mechanic note below).

**RUN C (2026-07-15) — N=3 shadow config, Thunder Spike Lv20 + Haunt Lv20 + a "+1 Shadow" slate:** Recount Average DPS 917 (2:00 span), Highest-5s 1066, Average-5s 832. This run's primary purpose was closing the Shadow Strike falloff-shape discriminator (full derivation in `data/verification/shadow-strike.json` — flat model matches within 0.3%, compounding model rejected by >8%); recorded here as the Thunder-Spike-side data point of the same measurement.

**Shadow cadence / stacking-structure observations (owner testimony + observation, 2026-07-15), on Thunder Spike's own inherent on-hit Numbed:**
- **1 shadow (dummy test):** Numbed alternates 1↔2 stacks, ~66% at 1 stack / ~33% at 2 (avg ≈1.33) — a different split from the Haunt (N=2, avg ≈1.5) run above, and the owner notes the split is partially attack-speed-dependent (any future model must derive it from attack speed, not hardcode a ratio).
- **Structure, even at 4 shadows/clones: inherent Numbed never exceeds 2 total stacks.** "1 sustained stack from the character's own True Body hit + at most 1 sustained stack from the shadows COLLECTIVELY" — i.e. all shadows pool into a single second inflict-source group, not one stack per shadow. Additional stacks beyond 2 require a genuinely separate inflict source (e.g. Numb Magnificent below, or a "+N Numbed stacks inflicted" line), and can then reach the glossary Numbed cap of 10.
- **Damage-threshold pathway ruled out:** the training dummy's Max Life+ES pool is enormous/unknown, so master_glossary 762's separate damage-threshold Numbed clause (1 stack per 10% of Max ES+Life dealt by Lightning Damage) cannot plausibly be firing at this damage level — it is NOT the source of the observed 2-stack structure; Thunder Spike's own dedicated on-hit line (see `formula`) is.

**Numb Magnificent (`thunder_spike_numb_magnificent`) sampling — still an unmodeled support, recorded here for future EV-model calibration (see also `data/verification/shadow-strike.json`):**
- 4 shadows: observed stacks ranging 1 through 9, possibly 10 (sampling limited, not a confirmed ceiling).
- 2 shadows: observed stacks ranging 1 through 6, mode ≈4 (6 rare).
- **Engine-side analysis (NOT a measurement):** `0.3 × shadow_hits_per_sec × 2s duration` predicts ≈+1.8 extra stacks at 2 shadows (mode ≈4 total with the 2 inherent) and ≈+3.6 extra at 4 shadows (avg ≈5.6, Poisson tail to 9–10) — both consistent with the sampled ranges. Supports the shape of the planned expected-stacks model; not yet engine-implemented.

## Derived / confirmed formula

`data/seasons/SS12/_skills.json` (`thunder_spike`): "Casts the skill and thrusts forward, dealing 277% Weapon Attack Damage" (205%→277% WAD across Lv1–20). Tags: Attack, Lightning, Area, Melee, Shadow Strike. Two inherent (non-optional) lines: "All of the skill's Physical Damage will be converted to Lightning Damage" (100% intrinsic Physical→Lightning) and "The skill's Shadow Strike True Body inflicts 1 stack of Numbed on enemies within a certain area on hit. Interval: 1s" (detailed_description: "within 1000 m of the enemy hit" — read as the game's large default AoE radius standing in for the skill's actual on-hit area, not a literal 1000m range). Support-line quotes (all sourced from `_skills.json`): **Thunder Spike: Rumbling Thunder (Noble)** — "When the supported skill's Shadow Strike True Body hits an enemy, +(45–48)% additional Lightning Damage dealt by the skill to the enemy for 2 s"; **Thunder Spike: Numb (Magnificent)** — "30% chance to inflict 1 stack of Numbed on enemies within a 10m radius when the supported skill's Shadows hit an enemy"; **Thunder Spike: Tremble (Noble)** — "The supported skill gains a buff on Critical Strike: +(66–71)% Numbed Effect for 2 s".

## Notes / caveats / open questions

**Supported (Tyra, 2026-07-15) — base WAD vs-target agreement**, and supporting evidence for the intrinsic Physical→Lightning conversion and inherent on-hit Numbed: solo engine 340.34 vs measured 349 (−2.5%, uncorrected — solo runs at a genuine flat 1 Numbed stack, so no correction applies); Haunt config engine 789.03 vs measured 810 (−2.6% at the flat-1-stack baseline, +0.1% corrected for the run's observed ~1.5-average Numbed stacks). See `dataPoints` for the full derivation, including the quantified Numbed-per-stack model (≈5.9%/stack at 18% Numbed Effect) and why check 2 (conversion + inherent Numbed) is only supported in aggregate, not isolated (this setup didn't test with conversion or Numbed suppressed). Rumbling Thunder was NOT socketed in this session (Setup B used Haunt, not Rumbling Thunder) — its default-ON assumption remains an unmeasured ASSUMPTION (Mercury-style caveat, unchanged): needs in-game confirmation of actual buff uptime behavior (does casting cadence realistically sustain the 2s window continuously?) and whether the buff is per-enemy or global.

**Mechanic STRUCTURE now known (owner-reported/observed, 2026-07-15), FORMULA still unmodeled: Shadow hits can themselves apply Thunder Spike's inherent on-hit Numbed**, not only the player's own True Body hit — this is how the Haunt run reaches an average ≈1.5 Numbed stacks (player's flat 1 + a shadow-applied stack, alternating 1↔2 with ~50% uptime on 2) while the solo (no-shadows) run stays at a genuine flat 1. Follow-up cadence testing (2026-07-15, see `dataPoints`) establishes the STRUCTURE: stacking is per-SOURCE-GROUP, not per-hit — 1 sustained stack from the character + at most 1 sustained stack from the shadows collectively, capped at 2 regardless of shadow count (observed to 4), with the 1-shadow case alternating 1↔2 at ~66%/~33% (avg ≈1.33), attack-speed-dependent (three calibration points so far across the two verification files: N=1 avg ≈1.33, N=2 avg ≈1.5, N=4 stays <2, approaching the structural cap). The engine's current flat-1-stack model (see `implementation`) is therefore exact for shadow-free configs and conservatively low (~−2.6% quantified here) once shadows are present; the clone-uptime FORMULA vs attack speed still needs a dedicated test at a different attack speed to calibrate before it can be engine-modeled. Filed alongside the shadow-hit-dependent NYI ledger in `data/verification/shadow-strike.json` (Numb Magnificent — now with sampled stack ranges, see `dataPoints` — and Frantic Shadow's Attack Speed proc) — same blocker, needs the clone-uptime formula plus shadow-hit-count/timing modeling to unlock. See `docs/BACKLOG.md` §0f.

**CONFOUND — documented for future tests, EXCLUDED for the 2026-07-15 runs (owner testimony, 2026-07-15).** The hero trait equipped in both runs, Erika's "Lightning Shadow" tier 1 (`data/seasons/SS12/_hero_traits.json:2718`), CAN itself inflict Numbed independently of Thunder Spike or Shadows: "Start moving … to gain 1 Electrify stack for every 3 m of movement made within the next 1 s, up to 3 stacks … When Electrify is owned, triggers Feline Figure on up to 3 enemies … For every 1 stack(s) of Electrify, Feline Figure inflicts 1 stack(s) of Numbed." **Owner confirms (2026-07-15) both RECOUNT runs were performed STATIONARY with NO Electrify buffs active (deliberately let them fall off before testing)** — so Feline Figure is EXCLUDED as the source of the Haunt run's second Numbed stack for these specific measurements; the observed 1↔2 alternation is correctly attributed to shadow-applied Numbed. This confound remains documented as something any FUTURE Thunder Spike test (with this trait equipped) must control for — confirm stationary / Electrify-inactive state — but SHADOW-01 check 6's isolation test no longer needs to re-litigate these two specific runs.

**Numb (Magnificent) — single-roll confirmed, doubled-line data artifact identified (owner tooltip screenshot, 2026-07-15).** At 1-star/Lv1, the owner's in-game tooltip shows the "30% chance to inflict 1 stack of Numbed on enemies within a 10m radius when the supported skill's Shadows hit an enemy" line appearing exactly ONCE. `data/seasons/SS12/_skills.json`'s `thunder_spike_numb_magnificent` entry (`description_lines`/`simple_description`, `raw_text` ~L139359) carries this line TWICE — once glued onto the "+20% additional damage for the supported skill" line, once again as its own standalone line. This is a **crawl/import artifact, NOT a second in-game roll** (a data-scraper investigation is being dispatched separately to fix the source). **Any future Numb Magnificent modeling must apply the 30% chance ONE time per Shadow hit, not twice.** For the record, the same tooltip also showed Mana Cost Multiplier 110.0% (matches `_skills.json`'s `mana_cost: "110.0%"`) and the T2 (level 2) roll "+(1–2)% additional damage" at 1-star (matches `_skills.json` `progression` level 2).

## Implementation (engine model)

Registered in `backend/engine/skill_resolver._REGISTRY` (was previously unregistered — a skill with no registry entry computes `total_dps=0.0`). **Intrinsic conversion (NEW mechanism)**: `ResolvedSkill.intrinsic_convert` (a `{src:{dst:frac}}` overlay merged into `offense._conversion_fracs`'s existing convert/adds-as cascade). This is the first skill-intrinsic conversion in the engine — the 2026-06-11 "Add outgoing damage-type conversion engine" commit explicitly deferred skill-intrinsic conversions, so there was no prior wiring to extend beyond the cascade itself. **Inherent Numbed-on-True-Body-hit**: `engine.ailment_inflict.scan_numbed_inflict` only scans gear/talent/custom-mod TEXT, not a skill's own inherent tooltip line, so it can't see this. Wired instead via a `thunder_spike`-scoped `ConditionEffect` pair (`enemy_numbed` set_true + `numbed_stacks` floor 1) appended to `inflict_cond_effects` in `server.py`, reusing the same `_apply_cond_effects` machinery curses use to auto-set `enemy_cursed`. `requires_dtype=None` (not "lightning") because attack-skill `ResolvedSkill.damage_types` is never populated (only spell resolvers set it) — Thunder Spike's Lightning damage is guaranteed unconditionally by its own 100% conversion, not a build choice. **Rumbling Thunder**: Noble/Magnificent supports do NOT go through `support_resolver.resolve_standard_supports`/`support_mapper.map_line` (`_STANDARD_TYPES` = support_skill/activation_medium_skill only) — they resolve via the separate `resolve_support_contributions`, whose specific-tier-line loop only recognized two fixed phrase shapes before this work. Added a third phrase branch (`"additional lightning damage dealt by the skill to the enemy"`) emitting `lightning_dmg_additional` gated by `condition_expr`, reached through the same `_split_condition` → `_COND_PATTERNS` → `_translate_condition_expr` gate every other tier line uses (new `_COND_PATTERNS` entry mapping the "Shadow Strike True Body hits an enemy" clause to a bare condition-key string `thunder_spike_true_body_buff`). Modeled as a **DEFAULT-ON** condition per owner instruction (`data/conditions.json` `thunder_spike_true_body_buff`, category "Buffs", `default_value: 1.0`): assumption is the player casts continuously vs a boss → ~permanent uptime, and "True Body" means the player's own cast, not a shadow.
